title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $9.03 sold 10 and 7 units (vs baseline 7.8), indicating a 10–25% drop in sales; no prior data at this price point, but consistent trend.

drivers.name: Supply risk (short delivery)
drivers.evidence: Planner note warns of potential supply issue; no prior occurrence, but plausible demand reduction due to out-of-stock risk.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.8. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased by 2.3% to $9.03, which is above the regular $8.83. Recent weeks at the new price (2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05) sold 10 and 7 units, both below baseline, suggesting a price sensitivity effect. The historical noise-adjusted lift from past promotions is only x1.16, but those were deeper discounts (up to 30%) and one was featured. The current price increase is likely to reduce demand. The supplier warning of a short delivery introduces supply risk, which may depress sales further. The uplift model suggests no effect, but judgment overrides it. A modest downside adjustment is warranted.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.8 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 23.4 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 16.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
